P8093.note: No single data center campus or tenant is named for this project. TC Energy approved the Northwoods expansion in May 2025 at about 900 million dollars to serve gas-fired power generation in the Midwest, including data centers and general economic growth. A Data Center Dynamics article from May 2025 says the added capacity is tied to 20 year take-or-pay contracts with Midwest utilities. A market note from East Daley Analytics, a gas market research firm, says Northwoods and the Guardian expansion together serve data center load growth and new utility generation in Illinois, Wisconsin and Michigan's Upper Peninsula. That note does not name a specific campus. The in-service date is late 2029.

batches/united-states-gas/staging/discov.note: The data center is Meta's campus in Middleton Township, Wood County, Ohio, near Bowling Green. A Cleanview profile says Meta owns it through a subsidiary called Liames LLC, under the code name Project Accordion. The campus is 715,000 square feet on 280 acres, with an investment of more than 800 million dollars, and it has been under construction since October 2024. Williams is building the Apollo power plant next to it, 350 MW of gas generation plus battery storage, owned through Will-Power OH LLC under a 10 year power purchase agreement with Meta. The Ohio Power Siting Board approved the plant on February 3, 2026 without a public hearing. Targets are the first 150 MW of generation in July 2027 and the full 350 MW in August 2027. A Bowling Green Independent Media report from July 2026 says Meta is the plant's only power customer and that the Apollo South Pipeline from the Rover Pipeline will fuel it, with construction targeted for September 2026. The February 2026 approval described gas supply as two 16-inch pipelines.

batches/united-states-gas/staging/discov.note: The data center is the EdgeConneX campus in New Albany, Licking County, Ohio. EdgeConneX bought 270 acres from VanTrust Real Estate for 137.2 million dollars. Phase 1 converts a 524,525 square foot warehouse and Phase 2 adds a 700,000 square foot data center. The campus is off-grid and powered by PowerConneX gas plants owned by an EdgeConneX affiliate. PowerConneX I is 120 MW and PowerConneX II is 216 MW, both under construction, and a third plant of 430 MW is in the pre-application stage. The Energy Cooperative of Newark is building the 24-mile line, and PowerConneX is paying about 160 million dollars for it. A Reporting Project article from July 2026 ties the line to the 216 MW plant. A Farm and Dairy article from June 2026 says the 430 MW plant would need a new 24-mile, 24-inch line. No tenant is named in the sources read. Phase 1 of the line is due in September 2027 and Phase 2 in 2028.

batches/united-states-gas/staging/discov.note: The data center is the Joule Capital Partners energy and data center campus in Millard County, Utah, about 145 miles south of Salt Lake City, on about 4,000 acres of former farmland. A Cleanview profile from January 2026 says the full build is 12 GW, with 455 MW targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026, 1.4 GW by 2027 and 5.8 GW by 2029. An August 2025 announcement cited 4 GW. The campus is off-grid and will generate its own power with Caterpillar gas engines and 1.1 GWh of battery storage. The profile says it will tie into the Kern River mainline through two redundant 36-inch connections. The county rezoned the land in August 2025 and groundbreaking was in November 2025. No tenant has been publicly named. The county notice for the 24-inch pipeline names only Joule as applicant, so the link to the campus is inferred.
